aspects.says: Dispatching over a CopyOnWriteArrayList or a copy taken first makes leaving safe: the leaver still gets the current event and no later one, and every other listener gets it.
basis: section:A Listener That Unsubscribes During a Dispatch Changes the List Being Walked

aspects.says: A listener that throws inside a plain loop ends the dispatch for every listener after it, and the exception reaches the publisher's caller.
basis: section:One Listener's Exception Skips the Listeners After It and Reaches the Publisher

aspects.says: A SubmissionPublisher cancels the subscription of a subscriber whose onNext throws and passes it the exception through onError, while other subscribers go on.
basis: section:When a Subscriber Can't Keep Up, a Flow Publisher Makes the Producer Wait or Drop
aspects.reason: one sentence on the JDK class's own behaviour; testing it means asynchronous delivery on the publisher's executor, which the page only mentions

aspects.says: A SubmissionPublisher bounds each subscriber's buffer: submit blocks the producer while it is full, offer hands what doesn't fit to a drop handler.
basis: section:When a Subscriber Can't Keep Up, a Flow Publisher Makes the Producer Wait or Drop

aspects.says: A subscribe that returns a handle owning its own entry removes exactly that registration on close, even when the same listener is subscribed more than once.
basis: section:A Listener Is Removed by the Reference It Was Added With, and a Second Lambda Is Another Object

aspects.says: The subject catches around each listener call and reports the failure where someone sees it, so the other listeners still run and the publisher returns normally.
basis: section:One Listener's Exception Skips the Listeners After It and Reaches the Publisher

aspects.says: A listener that removes itself while a for-each walks an ArrayList of listeners makes the dispatch throw ConcurrentModificationException or silently skip the listener after it, depending on where it sits.
basis: section:A Listener That Unsubscribes During a Dispatch Changes the List Being Walked

aspects.says: A listener never removed keeps its owner and everything the owner holds reachable for as long as the subject lives.
basis: section:The Subject Keeps Every Listener, and Everything It Captures, Until It Is Removed

aspects.says: Making publish synchronized calls every listener under the subject's lock, which can deadlock.
basis: section:A Listener That Unsubscribes During a Dispatch Changes the List Being Walked
aspects.reason: one clause pointing to unit 5.3.4, which shows the deadlock and has its own practice

aspects.says: java.util.Observable has been deprecated since Java 9; its javadoc points to java.beans, the concurrent collections and Flow.
basis: section:Design Note: Synchronous Dispatch Puts Every Listener's Cost on the Publisher
aspects.reason: a one-clause historical fact, not a behaviour a reader's code shows

aspects.says: java.beans.PropertyChangeSupport calls its listeners in one loop with no try, so one throwing listener stops the rest there too.
basis: section:One Listener's Exception Skips the Listeners After It and Reaches the Publisher
aspects.reason: a fact about a JDK class that the page shows by a run; the practice checks the reader's own subject, which is where the fix goes

aspects.says: A lambda or method reference written again is another object, so removing with it leaves the registered listener in place.
basis: section:A Listener Is Removed by the Reference It Was Added With, and a Second Lambda Is Another Object

aspects.says: A listener list that holds listeners weakly loses a lambda registered in place at the next collection, without an error.
basis: section:The Subject Keeps Every Listener, and Everything It Captures, Until It Is Removed
aspects.reason: when a weakly held listener is cleared depends on when the garbage collector runs, which no test can decide deterministically
